representations.text: Your 14-day window closely matched your 28-day baseline. Sleep averaged ~468 min vs ~471 min, with a consistent 07:00 wake time and slightly later bedtimes (~3 min). Steps (~7,954 vs ~8,066) and active minutes (~55) were stable. Resting heart rate dipped slightly to ~55.8 bpm. HRV RMSSD was mostly steady (~43 ms), but one night dropped to 23 ms before returning; this isolated reading may reflect measurement variability. Day-to-day patterns remained consistent.

In the recent 14 days, your resting heart rate rose notably from a baseline average of ~51.8 bpm to ~61.7 bpm, persisting throughout the window. Sleep duration (~472 min), steps (~7,923), active minutes (~56), low movement, and HRV RMSSD (~45 ms) all stayed near your 28-day baselines. Your sleep timing and 07:00 wake time were unchanged. The sustained RHR shift occurred without corresponding changes in other tracked metrics. Consider whether device fit or recording conditions changed.

For the first six days of your 14-day window, your metrics matched your 28-day baseline: sleep ~480 min starting ~22:40, waking at 07:00, steps ~7,976, active minutes ~56, RHR ~56 bpm, and HRV RMSSD ~45 ms. From April 6 onward, sleep start shifted past midnight (around 00:30–00:43), reducing recorded sleep to ~357–368 min while wake time stayed at 07:00. Steps, activity, RHR, and HRV remained at baseline levels. This pattern suggests truncated nighttime recording rather than a change in daytime metrics.

During your 14-day window, sleep duration increased slightly to ~478 min from a baseline of ~470 min. Your sleep schedule shifted: instead of a consistent ~22:50 bedtime and 07:00 wake, you alternated between earlier schedules (~22:15–06:30) and later ones (~00:40–09:00). Steps rose modestly (~8,052 vs ~7,940). Active minutes decreased slightly (~53 vs ~54). Resting heart rate (~56 bpm) and HRV RMSSD (~45 ms) remained near baseline. The new alternating sleep timing is the most notable change.
